                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The `observable` accepts a function that receives an `observer` which helps our link notify the next link up the chain how they should handle the operation result.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'In this function, we can just return `next(op)` and leave it as is, or we can subscribe to `next`, which enables our link to handle the operation result.\n'[39m +

                      [32m"console.log('performing operation:', op);\n"[39m +
                      [32m'const unsubscribe = next(op).subscribe({\n'[39m +
                      [32m'next(value) {\n'[39m +
                      [32m"console.log('we received value', value);\n"[39m +
                      [32m'observer.next(value);\n'[39m +

                      [32m"console.log('we received error', err);\n"[39m +

                      [32m'},\n'[39m +
                      [32m'});\n'[39m +
                      [32m'return unsubscribe;\n'[39m +
                      [32m'});\n'[39m +
                      [32m'};'[39m

                value: [
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# SuppressedError - JavaScript | MDN\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2025-07-30, last updated: 2026-03-23, [Read more](https://developer.mozilla.org/de/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/SuppressedError)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Das **`SuppressedError`**-Objekt repräsentiert einen Fehler, der beim Behandeln eines anderen Fehlers erzeugt wird.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Es wird während der Ressourcenverwaltung mit `using` oder `await using` generiert.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Im Vergleich zu `AggregateError` wird `SuppressedError` verwendet, um einen einzelnen Fehler darzustellen, der durch einen anderen Fehler unterdrückt wird, während `AggregateError` eine Liste von nicht zusammenhängenden Fehlern darstellt.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Es ist jedoch möglich, dass ein `SuppressedError` eine Kette von unterdrückten Fehlern enthält (`e.suppressed.suppressed.suppressed...`).\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Es unterscheidet sich auch semantisch von `cause`, da der Fehler nicht *durch* einen anderen Fehler verursacht wird, sondern *auftritt, während* ein anderer Fehler behandelt wird.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`SuppressedError` ist eine Unterklasse von `Error`.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- **`error`**\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Ein `SuppressedError` wird ausgelöst, wenn ein Fehler während der Ressourcenverwaltung auftritt.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Das Auslösen eines Fehlers verursacht das Bereinigen des Gültigkeitsbereichs, und jeder Disposer während der Bereinigung kann seinen eigenen Fehler auslösen.'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# SuppressedError - JavaScript - MDN Web Docs\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2026-01-21, last updated: 2026-06-05, [Read more](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/SuppressedError)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The SuppressedError object represents an error generated while handing another error.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'It is generated during resource disposal using using or await using.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Compared to AggregateError, SuppressedError represents an error that happened during the handling of another error, while AggregateError represents a list of unrelated errors.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'It is possible, though, for a SuppressedError to contain a chain of suppressed errors (e.suppressed.suppressed.suppressed...).\n'[39m +
                      [32m'It is also semantically different from cause because the error is not caused by another error, but happens when handling another error.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'SuppressedError is a subclass of Error.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'A SuppressedError is thrown when an error occurs during resource disposal.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Throwing an error causes scope cleanup, and each disposer during the cleanup can throw its own error.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'All these errors are collected into a chain of SuppressedError instances, with the original error as the suppressed property and the new error thrown by the next disposer as the error property.'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# SuppressedError() constructor - JavaScript | MDN\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2025-07-29, last updated: 2026-03-23, [Read more](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/SuppressedError/SuppressedError)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The **`SuppressedError()`** constructor creates `SuppressedError` objects.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'new SuppressedError(error, suppressed)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'new SuppressedError(error, suppressed, message)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'SuppressedError(error, suppressed)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'SuppressedError(error, suppressed, message)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'**Note:** `SuppressedError()` can be called with or without `new`.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Both create a new `SuppressedError` instance.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'### Parameters\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- **`error`**\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The new error that results in the suppression of `suppressed`.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- **`suppressed`**\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The error that was originally thrown and is now suppressed.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- **`message` Optional**\n'[39m +
                      [32m'An optional human-readable description of the aggregate error.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'**Note:** `SuppressedError()` does not accept `options` like `Error()` and other subclasses do, because the semantics of `cause` overlaps with `suppressed`.'[39m

                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Error Handling - Workers RPC\n'[39m +

                      [32m'An exception thrown by an RPC method implementation will propagate to the caller.\n'[39m +

                      [32m'created: 2025-01-31, last updated: 2025-12-31, [Read more](https://www.linkedin.com/learning/typescript-for-node-js-developers-25164739/introduction-to-suppressederror)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'[Instructor] In TypeScript 5.2, the SuppressedError has been introduced to handle case where multiple errors occur, particularly when an error is thrown during the disposal process of a resource, example using a Symbol.dispose method.\n'[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'IMPORTANT: This tool is for terminal operations like git, npm, docker, etc. DO NOT use it for file operations (reading, writing, editing, searching, finding files) - use the specialized tools for this instead.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Before executing the command, please follow these steps:\n'[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +

            [32m'  - If the commands depend on each other and must run sequentially, use a single executeCommand call with \'&&\' to chain them together (e.g., `git add . && git commit -m "message" && git push`).             [32m"  - Use ';' only when you need to run commands sequentially but don't care if earlier commands fail\n"[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'# Committing changes with git\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Only create commits when requested by the user. If unclear, ask first. When the user asks you to create a new git commit, follow these steps carefully:\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Git Safety Protocol:\n'[39m +
            [32m'- NEVER update the git config\n'[39m +
            [32m"- NEVER run destructive git commands (push --force, reset --hard, checkout ., restore ., clean -f, branch -D) unless the user explicitly requests these actions. Taking unauthorized destructive actions is unhelpful and can result in lost work, so it's best to ONLY run these commands when given direct instructions \n"[39m +

Instead, after hook failure, fix the issue, re-stage, and create a NEW commit\n'[39m +
